newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stronger vs dlr amid poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stronger vs dlr amid poor demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained marginally against the dollar on Friday, boosted by inflows in the face of poor demand, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.88 against the dollar from 54.91 on Thursday, while against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 87.40 from 87.81.
Dealers said inflows from foreign investors looking to buy treasury bills and a residue from agricultural exporters supported the shillings gains against the dollar.
"There's hardly any demand, which is why the market has simply responded by a marginally stronger shilling," one dealer said.
They said the shilling's bullish sentiment would continue at least for the short term, mostly because importers appeared to have shied off the market hoping to get a better price.
"The 54.85 level remains the key test for shilling strength," another dealer added.
The money market remained slightly short with overnight rates quoted above 15 percent unchanged. --Wambui Chege, Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261.
